uncategorised.reason: the parenthesised list itself; its elements carry `_argument`
the `...` marker: argument expansion in a call, grouping mode in a for-object. It marks how a neighbouring expression is used and denotes nothing itself
a backslash escape inside a quoted template; a heredoc has none, because its backslash is ordinary text

the possibly `::`-qualified name of a call — `provider::aws::arn_parse`. It cannot join `_name`, because `_name` is also the attribute-name and block-type position and HCL rejects `a::b` there; its own parts are `_name`, so a query for names still finds them
the delimiter word that closes a heredoc; the newline after it is not part of it, because HCL requires one and the attribute's own terminator is what consumes it
`<<EOT` or `<<-EOT` through the newline that ends the introduction; a delimiter, for `quote`'s reason
`key = value` inside an object literal — a position in a literal, not a declaration of the key

the `"` opening or closing a quoted template. A node rather than a hidden token because it must be external -- the scanner's template-mode stack opens and closes on it -- and an external token can be named or hidden but never anonymous; hiding a lexeme the language spells would put it nowhere in the tree

the parts of one branch of a template directive. Not `_body`, and the reason is mechanical rather than semantic: `_body` is also the block-body position, and a `_body` that admitted template text there would put `template_literal` in `valid_symbols` where a block's `{` is expected — at which point the scanner takes the `{` as literal text and the language stops parsing

the template `%{ if }` directive, and its `%{ for }` sibling is out for the same reason but is covered by `_scope` instead. Both are control flow and belong in `_branch` and `_loop` on the meaning; neither can be there in the parse table, because a supertype is ONE alternation, so putting the expression and template forms together makes `_control_flow` reachable at a template-part position AND as the start of a conditional's condition at that same position — `tree-sitter generate` rejects it as an unresolved conflict rather than accepting it as a widening. The terms went where the queries are: over Terraform, `(_branch)` and `(_loop)` are asked about the conditional and the for-expression

one RUN of literal text inside a template, between its interpolations and directives, with any escape sequences inside it. One node per run rather than per chunk, because that is the boundary hclsyntax's coalesced `LiteralValueExpr` draws and `treebank shape` checks
